# 易翼宗

## Authors / Editors
- 晏斯盛 (清朝) 撰

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

The canonical-commentary member of [晏斯盛](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%99%8F%E6%96%AF%E7%9B%9B) Yàn Sīshèng's three-part *Yì*-corpus, in six juàn. The work treats the canonical *Zhōuyì* scripture (sixty-four hexagrams' *Tuàn* and line statements), embedding Wing material under each canonical verse on a "scripture-explains-scripture" model — taking the Wings as the canonical authority *for* the *Yì* rather than as appendix *to* it. Each line is accompanied by a complete-hexagram diagram with one moving-line marked (odd as ○, even as a vertical mark) — Yàn's own typographic invention for marking the active line. Together with the *Xué Yì chū jīn* ([KR1a0147](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0147), the methodological framework) and the *Yì yì shuō* ([KR1a0149](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0149), the Wing-commentary), this forms the integrated middle volume of Yàn's *Yìxué* program.

The *Sìkù* editors' assessment is recorded in the joint tíyào at the head of [KR1a0147](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0147) (where the three-work corpus is treated together): the *Yì yì zōng* is methodologically distinctive but somewhat fragmenting; the typographic conventions are the author's "self-making-of-antiquity" but do not lapse into either the *fāngjì shùshù* technical-numerology or the empty *xīnxìng* metaphysical talk. The work is "still substantive-and-near-reason among recent *Yì*-houses."

**Abstract**

Composition is bracketed by Yàn's mid-Qiánlóng career; see [KR1a0147](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0147) for biographical details and the broader contextualization of the three-work *Yì*-corpus. The *Yì yì zōng* is the canonical-commentary middle member of the corpus, with the *Xué Yì chū jīn* (methodological framework) preceding and the *Yì yì shuō* (Wing commentary) following.

The work's principal methodological choice — embedding Wing material under each canonical verse — is one of several mid-Qīng experiments with the *gǔ Yì* / *jīn Yì* tension (cf. [KR1a0113](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0113) for an earlier hybrid approach; [KR1a0117](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR1/KR1a/KR1a0117) [李光地](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E6%9D%8E%E5%85%89%E5%9C%B0) Lǐ Guāngdì for the imperial *Zhé zhōng*'s *gǔ Yì* recovery). Yàn's solution differs from both: rather than separating the Wings as in *gǔ Yì* or interleaving them as in *jīn Yì*, he reads them downward into the canon at the level of each individual verse.
